concept.name: Gap
concept.definition: A blank space on a price chart where no trading occurred between two consecutive bars — typically when the open of one session is entirely above the prior session's high (up gap) or below its low (down gap). Gaps are classified (common, breakaway, runaway, exhaustion) by location and context; the classifications are interpretive, not mechanical laws.
concept.intuition: Overnight news or sentiment shifts the supply-demand balance so much that the market has to reopen at a different price entirely, skipping the levels in between.
concept.mechanics: Detected by comparing one bar's range to the next: an up gap requires the new session's low to exceed the prior session's high; a down gap requires the new session's high to fall below the prior session's low. Significance is judged by size, volume, and position within the trend or pattern.
concept.failure_modes: Gap-type labels are only reliably assignable in hindsight (an exhaustion gap looks like a runaway gap when it prints); the popular belief that 'all gaps get filled' fails badly for breakaway and runaway gaps.
concept.misconceptions: That every gap must soon be filled; waiting for breakaway or runaway gaps to fill can mean missing or fighting an entire trend leg.
concept.example: A stock closes at 50, reports strong earnings after the bell, and opens the next day at 54, never trading below 53.8: the 50-53.8 void is an up gap.

citations.source: StockCharts ChartSchool — Gaps and Gap Analysis
